extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners and parties in AIA proceedings (patent owners, petitioners, counsel appearing before the PTAB)
extracted.subtask_short: PTAB director review and MTA rules
extracted.subtask_description: Extracts procedural and substantive rules for requesting Director Review, filing and resolving Motions to Amend, and updated rules on admission/pro hac vice practice before the PTAB in AIA proceedings. Focuses on deadlines, content/format limits, burdens of persuasion, Board discretion, evidence rules, and representation rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of Director Review (Section 42.75(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: A party may only request Director Review of: a decision on whether to institute an AIA trial; a final decision in an AIA proceeding; a panel decision granting a request for rehearing of a decision on whether to institute a trial or a final decision in an AIA proceeding; or any other decision concluding an AIA trial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For purposes of this section, the term 'final decision' is defined as a 'final decision' under 35 U.S.C. § 135 as well as a 'final written decision' under 35 U.S.C. §§ 318 or 328. The final rules also explicitly include derivations and decisions terminating AIA proceedings other than a final written decision (e.g., adverse judgment or dismissal).

rubrics_metrics.name: Director sua sponte review timing (Section 42.75(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director may grant review sua sponte.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Initiation of sua sponte review will be within 21 days after expiration of the period for filing a request for rehearing, pursuant to § 42.71(d), absent exceptional circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit on number/timing of Director Review requests (Section 42.75(c) & (c)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: A party to a proceeding under part 42 may file one request for Director Review of a decision as provided in paragraph (a) instead of filing a request for rehearing, subject to limitations and Director guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A request for Director Review must be filed within the time period set forth in § 42.71(d) unless an extension is granted by the Director upon a showing of good cause.

rubrics_metrics.name: Format, length, and new evidence prohibition for Director Review requests (Section 42.75(c)(2)-(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests are subject to length limitations (i.e., 15 pages) and formatting requirements; no new evidence may be submitted unless authorized by the Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Length limitation: 15 pages per 37 C.F.R. § 42.24(a)(1)(v). Formatting: 37 C.F.R. § 42.6(a). Submission details and any additional implementation guidance are available on the Director Review webpage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final agency decision effect and exceptions (Section 42.75(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: A decision on institution, a final decision, or a decision granting rehearing of such a decision shall become the final agency decision unless a party requests rehearing or Director Review within the prescribed time or the Director initiates sua sponte review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upon denial of a request for Director Review of a final decision (or rehearing of a final decision), the Board’s decision becomes the final agency decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of Director Review on underlying proceeding and record (Section 42.75(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for Director Review or initiation of review does not stay the time for parties to take action in the underlying proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the Director grants review, the Director will issue an order or decision that will be made part of the public record, subject to protective orders or other confidentiality requirements. If the Director grants review and does not withdraw the grant, the review concludes with issuance of a reasoned decision or order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appealability and timing resets (Section 42.75(e)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: A Director Review decision of a final decision (or equivalent appealable decision) is appealable using the same procedures under 35 U.S.C. §§ 141(c), 141(d), 319.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A request for Director Review (or sua sponte initiation) will be treated as a request for rehearing and will reset the time for appeal until after all issues on Director Review are resolved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director delegation authority (Section 42.75(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director may delegate their review of a decision provided in paragraph (a), subject to any conditions the Director provides.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Delegation may occur and the rules record statistics showing some requests were delegated; parties should monitor Director guidance for any delegation conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ex parte communications and third-party communications rule (Section 42.75(g))
rubrics_metrics.description: All communications from a party to the Office concerning a specific Director Review request or proceeding must copy counsel for all parties; communications from third parties regarding a specific Director Review request or proceeding, aside from authorized amicus briefing, are not permitted and will not be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure counsel for all parties are copied on communications. Unauthorized third-party communications will be disregarded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing assistance and status resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Designated channels exist for filing help and Director Review-specific inquiries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For PTACTS/filing issues: Trials@uspto.gov or 571-272-7882. For Director Review-specific issues: Director_PTABDecision_Review@uspto.gov (always copy counsel for all parties). Director Review status page maintained at www.uspto.gov/patents/patent-trial-and-appeal-board/status-director-review-requests; parties should consult the Director Review webpage for implementation details before the effective date.

rubrics_metrics.name: MTA Pilot Program permanence (37 C.F.R. §§ 42.121, 42.221)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Motion to Amend Pilot Program is made permanent by the final rule; the final rule implements MTA procedures in IPR (§ 42.121) and PGR (§ 42.221).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The final rule (published Sept 18, 2024) makes pilot options permanent and effective Oct 18, 2024; the Board will continue to apply pilot timelines for briefs and allows specified deadline extensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent owner burden on motions to amend (37 C.F.R. § 42.121(d)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent owner bears the burden of persuasion to show, by a preponderance of the evidence, that the motion to amend complies with statutory and regulatory requirements (including paragraphs (1) and (3) of 35 U.S.C. 316(d) and paragraphs (a)(2) and (3) and (b)(1) and (2) of the section).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific statutory/regulatory components include showing a reasonable number of proposed substitute claims; that substitute claims respond to a ground of unpatentability; that proposed substitute claims do not enlarge the scope of the claims; and that the motion does not introduce new matter. These burden-allocation rules were unchanged from the 2021 revisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petitioner burden on motions to amend (37 C.F.R. § 42.121(d)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: A petitioner bears the burden of persuasion to show, by a preponderance of the evidence, that any proposed substitute claims are unpatentable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitioner must present prior art/arguments sufficient to satisfy preponderance for anticipation or obviousness (and may raise issues such as eligibility, indefiniteness, or enablement where appropriate).

rubrics_metrics.name: Board discretion to raise a new ground of unpatentability (37 C.F.R. § 42.121(d)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: Irrespective of the parties' burdens, the Board may exercise its discretion to grant or deny a motion to amend or to raise a new ground of unpatentability in connection with a proposed substitute claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where the Board exercises this discretion to raise a new ground, the parties will have notice and an opportunity to respond. In exercising this discretion, the Board may consider all evidence of record in the proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board may add evidence from related proceedings and judicially noticed district court evidence (37 C.F.R. § 42.121(d)(3)(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board may consider and make of record any evidence in a related proceeding before the Office and evidence that a district court can judicially notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This expands the evidence the Board may add beyond the previous limitation to only readily identifiable and persuasive evidence of record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board-requested examination assistance and use of results (37 C.F.R. § 42.121(d)(3)(ii))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board may request examination assistance and consider information identified in response, and make that information part of the record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Board may request examination assistance at any time after any motion to amend has been filed if no petitioner opposes or all petitioners cease to oppose a motion to amend, or if the Board determines a deficient prior art challenge warrants a search for additional prior art. The Board is not required to request examination assistance even if there is no opposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Removal of prior qualifiers on Board discretion and evidence (rule changes to (d)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: The final rule removes prior qualifiers such as 'interests of justice' and the limitation that Board-added reasons/evidence be 'only for reasons supported by readily identifiable and persuasive evidence of record.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Board now has broader discretion to raise new grounds and to make additional types of evidence part of the record; new Board evidence need not be 'readily identifiable and persuasive.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard for Board determination on a new ground of unpatentability (37 C.F.R. § 42.121(d)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the Board exercises its discretion under paragraph (d)(3), the Board must determine unpatentability based on a preponderance of the evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This codifies the applicable evidentiary standard for any Board-raised unpatentability determination in connection with an MTA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary Guidance and Revised Motion to Amend provisions (37 C.F.R. § 42.121(e),(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: The rule formally recognizes Preliminary Guidance (PG) from the Board and permits Revised Motions to Amend following PG or petitioner opposition; also adds timing for PG requests and accounts for revised MTAs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent owners may request Preliminary Guidance and may file a revised MTA after receiving petitioner’s opposition and/or Board PG. The rule describes deadline extensions possible upon receiving PG or a revised MTA, and the Board will continue to apply pilot timelines for briefs.

rubrics_metrics.name: MTA procedural structure retained (timing, listing support, additional MTA)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior rule structure retained in substance: (a) timing, scope, number of substitute claims; (b) listing of substitute claims and support in disclosures; (c) additional MTA; (d) parties' burden of persuasion and Board discretion (with changes reflected in final rule).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section (b) and (c) are substantively unchanged in the final rule; practitioners should follow the established listing/support requirements when drafting MTAs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board may act on deficient petitioner challenges by searching additional prior art
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Board determines that a petitioner's prior art challenge in an opposition to a motion to amend is deficient, it may request examination assistance to search for additional prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Board-requested examination assistance and the results will be made of record; used when petitioner opposition is deficient or when no petitioner opposes/all cease opposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pro hac vice and representation changes (Final rules on expanding opportunities)
rubrics_metrics.description: Final rules permit parties to proceed without separate back-up counsel upon a showing of good cause; create a new, streamlined and fee-free procedure for pro hac vice admission for attorneys who have previously been recognized by the Board; and clarify the disclosure duties of those admitted pro hac vice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effective Nov 12, 2024. In response to stakeholder input, the Office is not adopting a final rule permitting non-registered attorneys admitted pro hac vice to serve as lead counsel at this time; instead the Office will explore a pilot project permitting non-registered counsel to serve as lead counsel in some circumstances and may consider a future rule change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural notice and stakeholder engagement (NPRM/comments/statistics)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office sought public comment (NPRMs) and considered commenter suggestions (e.g., to add standards of review, allow extensions, allow sur-reply, clarify written description identification), and provided statistics on requests/grants/denials to inform implementation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters suggested formal standards of review and other changes; the Office declined to codify a standard of review at this time but provided standards on the Director Review webpage. Parties should consult the Director Review webpage for current implementation details.
